facts.value: Type identifies new, amended or repealed statutes; Bill identifies Senate or House bills, numbered from 1 and 2001 respectively; Sec is the bill section; SL Ch is the 2026 session-law chapter except in the specified delayed-section tables. O gives the reading order for multiple amendments. Thus entries 51 and 92 are Senate bills.
facts.supporting_quote: Bill - includes Senate Bills (commencing with SB Number 1) and House Bills (commencing with HB Number 2001).

facts.value: The act takes effect upon publication in the statute book; the enrolled text does not supply a dated approval.
facts.locator: Operative legislative HTML rendering, section 9 and approval block
facts.supporting_quote: This act shall take effect and be in force from and after its publication in the statute book.

facts.value: Both are listed as effective July 1, 2026, in 2026 session-law chapter 153: section 1 creates K.S.A. 75-7247; section 2 amends K.S.A. 46-1135.

facts.value: Both are listed as effective July 1, 2026, in 2026 session-law chapter 153: section 3 amends K.S.A. 75-4704; section 4 amends K.S.A. 75-4705.

facts.field: Official section dates and mapping: sections 5–6

facts.field: Official section date and mapping: section 7
facts.value: Section 7 amends K.S.A. 75-7205 and is listed as effective July 1, 2026, in 2026 session-law chapter 153, reading order 3. All seven substantive sections therefore carry the same listed date.
The Revisor lists one amended statutory section: section 1 amends K.S.A. 66-1,184, 2026 session-law chapter 113, effective July 1, 2026.

facts.value: July 1, 2027 is the expiration date for K.S.A. 66-1,184 subsection (i), concerning specified large-load customers and historic peak demand—not the expiration of the entire act.
facts.locator: Operative legislative HTML rendering, section 1, subsection (i)(1)–(3)
facts.supporting_quote: The provisions of this subsection shall expire on July 1, 2027.

facts.value: July 1, 2030 is the expiration date for subsection (d)(4), concerning specified methods of determining compensation for exported energy.
facts.locator: Operative legislative HTML rendering, section 1, subsection (d)(4)
facts.supporting_quote: The provisions of this paragraph shall expire on July 1, 2030.

facts.value: Subsection (h) specifies aggregate export-capacity thresholds of 6% from July 1, 2025, 7% from July 1, 2026, and 8% from July 1, 2027 and each year thereafter. Subsection (i) uses July 1, 2025 as the relevant service-commencement threshold for specified facilities.
facts.locator: Operative legislative HTML rendering, section 1, subsections (h)(1) and (i)(1)–(2)
facts.supporting_quote: Commencing on July 1, 2025, 6% ... commencing on July 1, 2026, 7% ... commencing on July 1, 2027, and each year thereafter, 8%

facts.value: The Department of Revenue says SB 98 passed and was signed during the 2025 session, and that its provisions take effect upon publication in the statute book. The notice does not give the signature date.
facts.supporting_quote: During the 2025 Legislative Session Senate Bill 98 was passed and signed into law. ... The provisions of Senate Bill 98 take effect and are in force from and after publication in the statute book.

facts.field: Program eligibility start and statutory mapping
facts.value: K.S.A. 74-50,333(a) states that on and after July 1, 2025 a qualified firm meeting the referenced requirements may be eligible. Its history identifies 2025 session-law chapter 124, section 3, with a July 1 date.
facts.supporting_quote: On and after July 1, 2025, a qualified firm that meets the requirements ... may be eligible for a sales tax exemption ... History: L. 2025, ch. 124, § 3; July 1.

facts.field: Qualified-purchase date and additional statutory mapping
facts.value: The Revenue notice says the K.S.A. 79-3606 exemption applies to qualified purchases made on or after July 1, 2025. It identifies SB 98 section 5 as amending K.S.A. 66-101j and section 6 as amending K.S.A. 79-3606.
facts.supporting_quote: The new sales tax exemption found in K.S.A. 79-3606 applies to qualified purchases made on or after July 1, 2025.

facts.value: The program date does not itself establish approval for an individual firm: the secretary of revenue may not approve an exemption without certification by the secretary of commerce. The statute states a 20-year period after commencement of operations.
facts.supporting_quote: No sales tax exemption shall be approved by the secretary of revenue unless the qualified firm has been certified by the secretary of commerce

The SB 92 rendering removes semantic strike tags. It establishes one substantive amended statutory section and the displayed July 1, 2027 sunset, but does not by itself reliably establish the prior sunset date or the full set of textual changes.
No supplied source identifies an individual firm's certification or approval date. The sources do not establish current force or entitlement to benefits.
The supplied SB 98 sources expressly map section 3 to chapter 124 and K.S.A. 74-50,333, but do not provide a complete Revisor mapping for every SB 98 section.

field_decisions.value: Enrolled act created a qualified data center sales tax exemption for construction, equipment, eligible costs and certain labor, subject to a $250 million investment commitment, jobs and other conditions; eligible costs exclude electricity. It also limits a specified economic-development electric-rate discount and requires fusion-center review and approval before public financial assistance or benefits. K.S.A. 74-50,333(a) and Revenue Notice 25-03 apply the exemption to qualified purchases made on or after July 1, 2025; approval still requires Commerce certification.
field_decisions.reason: Section 74-50,333(a) sets eligibility on and after July 1, 2025; the Revenue notice states that the exemption applies to qualified purchases on or after that date. Section 74-50,333(c) requires Commerce certification before Revenue approval. This is a provision-specific statement, not a normalized whole-act date or evidence that any individual firm received benefits.
